thread:
alex_sales: FYI customer (FinData) is asking for a commit + POC. They want guidance on reserved GPU counts + autoscale prewarm/burst behavior. estimated profile: 500 req/min, avg 60 tokens per req, p50 latency target 250ms.

maria_solutions: quick q — is that 500 concurrent or 500/min? big diff for batching.

alex_sales: 500 requests per minute sustained, with bursts up to 1200/min for 10m windows during trading opens.

ram_engineer: ok that's ~8.3 r/s sustained, bursts to 20 r/s. tokens/s sustained ~500 * 60 / 60 = 500 t/s? wait math: 500 req/min * 60 tokens = 30k tokens/min -> 500 tokens/s. bursts ~1200*60/60=1200 t/s.

sophie_pm: they want guaranteed throughput for market hours. also care about cost predictability for commit pricing.

maria_solutions: recommendation sketch: reserved pool sized for sustained rps + a small hedged pool for bursts. We can use autoscale but need warmup/queueing considerations for GPU spin-up.

ram_engineer: exact numbers: for the model they plan to use (redwood-bert-large-quant), our perf profile says ~45 tokens/s per GPU for p50<250ms with batching. So to hit 500 t/s sustained we'd need ~12 GPUs. For 1200 t/s bursts, ~27 GPUs.

jess_ops: note: autoscale spin-up from zero -> GPU takes ~4-6 minutes in Dedicated (provision + model load). not suitable for 10m bursts. we recommend warm pool of idle instances or prewarmed containers.

alex_sales: customer asked whether commit can be structured with base reserved and burst credits — can we offer a model?

cost_bot: @alex_sales templated answer: Offer a Reserved Base (12 GPUs) + Burst Credits (equivalent to 15 GPUs hours per day) and an autoscale policy with prewarm pool of N nodes. Pricing: base commit at 80% discount vs on-demand, burst credits at blended rate.

maria_solutions: operationally: prewarm pool should be sized to cover typical bursts (here ~15 GPUs) and be billed as reserved/burst depending on contract. Also set fallback model variants (smaller quantized) to degrade gracefully if prewarm exhausted.

ram_engineer: add: KV/prefix cache helps a lot if requests are similar — effective tokens/s per GPU can jump 1.5x. we should ask FinData for request similarity and prompt reuse.

sophie_pm: let's draft the POC plan for engineering sign-off:
- Phase 1: baseline perf run with their sample traffic (30m) on hosted dev cluster to validate tokens/s numbers
- Phase 2: dedicated reserve sizing (12 GPUs) + prewarm 15 GPUs to simulate bursts
- Phase 3: test fallback (quantized small model) and measure quality delta

alex_sales: customer also wants to know about billing for prewarm — charged as reserved or as burst?

jess_ops: depends on contract. we can structure prewarm as part of the reserved capacity (kept hot) or as billable burst credits. Legal prefers clearer SLAs if it's part of reserved capacity.

maria_solutions: for the SLO (250ms p50) we should insist on a canary traffic policy + automatic fallback if latency climbs beyond threshold. we can configure that in the rollout.

ram_engineer: technical blocker: their security team wants no egress to public internet for model download. Private deployment needed for on-prem model preload. that adds ~2-3 hours setup per node for image and model staging — less ideal for ad-hoc burst.

alex_sales: ok customer will need Private or Dedicated with VPC model preload. flagging for legal/compliance.

sophie_pm: next steps for sales collateral: create a sample commit proposal showing numbers and two options: (A) base reserved 12 GPUs + prewarm 15 GPUs (hot) billed as reserved; (B) base reserved 12 GPUs + burst credits + 1 GPU warm pool, plus fallback model. Include cost delta and risk table.

maria_solutions: I'll draft the playbook. can someone share the perf artifacts for redwood-bert-large-quant and the KV cache numbers?

ram_engineer: sharing perf snippet:```
model: redwood-bert-large-quant
hw: A100-40GB
batch dist: dynamic, avg batch 10
steady: 45 tok/s/GPU @ p50 230ms
with_kv_cache: ~70 tok/s/GPU
```

alex_sales: perfect. I'll send FinData the two-option doc and ask for sample traffic and similarity KPI.

jess_ops: FYI — bumping prewarm count impacts capacity planning for the region; we should run this against our region quota. I can run a quota check if you want.

maria_solutions: please run quota check and also a quick runbook for failover: region fallback -> smaller model -> degrade quality gracefully.

alex_sales: thanks team. I'll schedule a POC kickoff w/ FinData for Wed next week. tagging this thread for followups. :shipit:
